info.title: Canonical Excel model extraction, diff and benchmarking
info.description: ExcelCannon - fast Rust-powered tooling for reading, diffing, and generating Excel workbooks. Native binary packaged for win-x64 and linux-x64 (glibc 2.17 or newer); macOS is on the roadmap.

commands.name: diff
commands.description: Compare two workbooks (or extracted models) and score the differences

options.name: --json
options.description: Also write the machine-readable report here

options.name: --epsilon
options.description:
Absolute tolerance when comparing numeric values
[default: 0.000000001]

options.name: --weights
options.description:
How much each category contributes to the overall score.
Defaults: `value=0.4,formula=0.3,structure=0.2,format=0.1`. A category this does not name keeps its default, so `--weights format=0` is the whole of "stop letting cell styling drag the headline down".
The four are ratios, renormalized over the categories the two workbooks actually exercised, and the effective weighting is stamped on the report so two differently-weighted runs cannot be compared by accident. Refused: a name that is not one of the four, a negative weight, and four zeros.

options.name: --top-n
options.description:
Findings listed per sheet and category in the human summary.
Markdown only, and per (sheet, category) group. It never changes `--json`'s `findings` array — use `--finding-limit-per-category` for that, which bounds the report itself; this then caps what the markdown lists out of whatever that report already carries.
[default: 50]

options.name: --finding-limit-per-category
options.description:
Findings the machine-readable report carries, per category, across the whole workbook.
Unlike `--top-n`, this changes the report itself: `--json` carries at most this many findings of each category, and the report states what it left out under `truncation`. The scores, the exit code and `not compared` are computed on the full comparison and are untouched. `0` keeps the summary and no findings at all.

options.name: --error-format
options.description:
How to report a failure on stderr.
Spelled `--error-format` rather than `--json` because `diff --json FILE` and `lint --json FILE` already mean "write the *report* there"; this is global, so it also reaches `extract`, which has no report flag at all.
Possible values:
- text: A human-readable block: the code and category, then the context
- json: One line of JSON, for a script to parse. Stdout stays data-only
[default: text]

options.name: --exclude-finding-category
options.description:
Leave this category's findings out of the report entirely. Repeatable.
One of `value`, `formula`, `format`, `structure`. Diagnostics and scoring are separate concerns, so `--weights format=0` never suppresses a finding on its own; this is how a caller who has deliberately excluded an axis from the score stops paying for its evidence too. Excluding every category still exits 1 when the two sides differ.

options.name: --sheet
options.description: Read, compare or check only this sheet. Repeatable

options.name: --timeout
options.description:
Seconds a download may take, end to end
[default: 60]

options.name: --exclude-sheet
options.description: Skip this sheet. Repeatable, and not combinable with `--sheet`/`--region`

options.name: --max-download
options.description:
Megabytes a download may reach before it is refused
[default: 200]

options.name: --allow-insecure-http
options.description:
Allow a plain `http://` source URL.
Off by default. A presigned URL's query string is a credential, and an unencrypted request hands it to anybody on the path.

options.name: --region
options.description:
Read, compare or check only this range of this sheet: `--region "3a. BENEFITS!A1:W382"`.
Repeatable, and combinable with `--sheet` for the sheets that are wanted whole — but not for the same sheet, which would be asking for it both ways at once. Quote a sheet name as a formula would.

commands.name: extract
commands.description: Extract a workbook into the canonical JSON model

options.name: --mode
options.description:
How much to keep: template structure, structure plus values, or structure plus column schemas with the data suppressed
Possible values:
- template: Structure and literals, without cached formula results
- data:     Everything, cached results included
- schema:   Structure and a column schema per region; no data-region values
[default: template]

options.name: --data
options.description: Alias for `--mode data`

options.name: --header
options.description:
Declare a header row the detector should trust: `--header "Sheet!A7"`.
Repeatable. The row of the named cell is read as a header for the rows beneath it, ahead of every heuristic — including the workbook's own table parts. Only the row matters; the column is ignored. Quote a sheet name that needs it, as a formula would: `--header "'Q3 data'!A7"`.
Pointed at a row of data this publishes that row, so point it at a header row.

options.name: --distinct-values
options.description:
Publish the distinct values of low-cardinality columns in schema mode.
Off by default: schema mode's promise is counts-not-values, and this is the one deliberate exception to it. With no number the threshold is 12; `--distinct-values=30` raises it; `0` is the same as omitting the flag. Sets are withheld regardless of cardinality when the values look like identifiers or repeat too little to be a vocabulary.

options.name: --withhold-name
options.description:
Withhold a column or field by name in schema mode. Repeatable.
Matched exact and case-fold only, after trimming: `Member DOB` matches `member dob` and does not match `DOB`, `Member D.O.B.` or `MemberDOB`. There is no fuzzy matching of any kind — see issue #33, whose fuzzier matcher this deliberately declines to be. The header and the label are kept — a consumer needs to know the column exists — and the column's distinct set and its resolved vocabulary go.

options.name: --error-format
options.description:
How to report a failure on stderr.
Spelled `--error-format` rather than `--json` because `diff --json FILE` and `lint --json FILE` already mean "write the *report* there"; this is global, so it also reaches `extract`, which has no report flag at all.
- text: A human-readable block: the code and category, then the context
- json: One line of JSON, for a script to parse. Stdout stays data-only
[default: text]

options.name: --withhold-names
options.description:
Read withheld names from a file, one per line. Unions with `--withhold-name`.
UTF-8; a leading byte-order mark, blank lines, and lines whose first non-space character is `#` are skipped.

options.name: --out
options.description: Write the canonical JSON model here instead of to stdout

options.name: --timeout
options.description:

[default: 60]

options.name: --max-download

[default: 200]

options.name: --text

options.name: --allow-insecure-http
options.description:
Allow a plain `http://` source URL.
Off by default. A presigned URL's query string is a credential, and an unencrypted request hands it to anybody on the path.

options.name: --section
options.description:
Render only this section. Repeatable.
One of `input-surface`, `names`, `geometry`, `styles`, `cells`, `fills`, `tables`, `validations`, `condfmt`, `charts`, `headers`, `schemas`, `deps`, `vba` — or the group `surface`, the writable contract (labels, types, vocabularies) with no grid, no styling and no dependency summary. Not combinable with `--exclude-section`.

options.name: --exclude-section
options.description: Render every section except this one. Repeatable, and not combinable with `--section`

options.name: --sheet
options.description: Read, compare or check only this sheet. Repeatable

options.name: --exclude-sheet
options.description: Skip this sheet. Repeatable, and not combinable with `--sheet`/`--region`

options.name: --region
options.description:
Read, compare or check only this range of this sheet: `--region "3a. BENEFITS!A1:W382"`.
Repeatable, and combinable with `--sheet` for the sheets that are wanted whole — but not for the same sheet, which would be asking for it both ways at once. Quote a sheet name as a formula would.

options.name: --batch
options.description:
Read a list of workbooks from FILE — one path or `https://` URL per line — and extract every one of them, writing one aggregate report instead of one model.
Blank lines are skipped, as is a line whose first non-whitespace character is `#`; neither consumes an entry index. `-` reads the list from stdin. Every option above except `--out`/`--text` (which conflict with this one) applies identically to every entry — this runs one fixed set of extract options over many workbooks, not a way to vary them per file. A workbook that cannot be read does not stop the run; its entry is recorded as failed and the rest still run. See `docs/errors.md`, "Batch mode", for the exit-code contract.

options.name: --json
options.description:
Write the batch's aggregate report here. Only valid with `--batch`.
Not a clap `requires`: with `path` present (the common case, since it is only optional so `--batch` can stand in for it), clap 4.6's requirement resolution does not enforce a plain `requires` on another field — checked explicitly at the top of [`extract`] instead, in the same `usage_error` shape `--distinct-values` already uses.

options.name: --out-dir
options.description: With `--batch`, write each entry's model here, named `NNNN-<stem>.json`. Without `--out-dir` a batch run writes no models at all — only the aggregate report. See `json`'s doc comment for why this is not a clap `requires`

options.name: --text-dir
options.description: With `--batch`, also write each entry's text rendering here, named `NNNN-<stem>.txt`. See `json`'s doc comment for why this is not a clap `requires`

options.name: --fail-fast
options.description:
With `--batch`, stop after the first entry that fails to extract.
Off by default: a corpus sweep must not stop because one workbook is password-protected. The aggregate is still written when this stops the run early, holding exactly the entries that ran. See `json`'s doc comment for why this is not a clap `requires`.

options.name: --help
options.description: Print help (see a summary with '-h')

arguments.name: PATH
arguments.description:
Workbook to read: a path (`.xlsx`, `.xlsm` or `.xlsb`) or an `https://` URL.
A presigned Azure Blob or S3 URL works as it stands — the query string is what authenticates it. Its signature is never printed, logged or written into the model.
Optional only because `--batch` reads a list of these from a file instead; every other invocation requires it.

commands.name: lint
commands.description: Check one workbook (or extracted model) against the lint rules

options.name: --json
options.description: Also write the machine-readable report here. With `--batch` this is the batch's aggregate report rather than one workbook's

options.name: --batch
options.description:
Read a list of workbooks from FILE — one path or `https://` URL per line — and lint every one of them, writing one aggregate report.
Blank lines are skipped, as is a line whose first non-whitespace character is `#`; neither consumes an entry index. `-` reads the list from stdin. `--strict`, `--rule`/`--exclude-rule` and the scope flags apply identically to every entry. A workbook that cannot be read does not stop the run; its entry is recorded as failed and the rest still run. See `docs/errors.md`, "Batch mode", for the exit-code contract.

options.name: --fail-fast
options.description:
With `--batch`, stop after the first entry that fails to load.
Off by default, for the same reason `extract --batch`'s twin is: a corpus sweep must not stop because one workbook is password-protected. Findings never trigger this — only an entry this tool could not read at all does. Not a clap `requires` — see [`ExtractArgs::json`]'s doc comment for why — and checked explicitly at the top of [`lint`] instead.

options.name: --strict
options.description: Fail on warnings and notices as well as on errors

options.name: --top-n
options.description:
Findings listed per rule in the human summary.
Per rule rather than in total, so one flooding rule cannot push the others off the end of the report. The JSON always carries them all.
[default: 50]

options.name: --error-format
options.description:
How to report a failure on stderr.
Spelled `--error-format` rather than `--json` because `diff --json FILE` and `lint --json FILE` already mean "write the *report* there"; this is global, so it also reaches `extract`, which has no report flag at all.
Possible values:
- text: A human-readable block: the code and category, then the context
- json: One line of JSON, for a script to parse. Stdout stays data-only
[default: text]

options.name: --rule
options.description:
Run only this rule. Repeatable. See `--list-rules`.
An id that is not a rule is refused rather than ignored: a gate whose typo silently ran nothing would report a clean workbook having checked none of it.

options.name: --exclude-rule
options.description:
Skip this rule. Repeatable, and not combinable with `--rule`.
Spelled `--exclude-rule` rather than `--disable-rule` for one reason: `--exclude-sheet` is already the word this tool uses for "everything except these".

arguments.name: OLD
arguments.description: The older generation: a path or an `https://` URL, a raw workbook or an extracted model

arguments.name: NEW
arguments.description:
The newer generation, under the same rule as `old`.
Named `old`/`new` rather than `left`/`right`: unlike `diff`, direction is load-bearing here — `label_change`, `constraint_change` and the rest all read as "what `old` had before" and "what `new` has now".

commands.name: render
commands.description: Render an extracted model as compact text

options.name: --mode
options.description:
Which reading the model was extracted as. Only `data` renders cached formula results, which is the one thing the rendering can withhold.
Omitted, the rendering withholds them, exactly as it always has. Given and disagreeing with the model's own `kind`, the mismatch is stated on stderr: what was *stated* still decides, so `--mode template` over a data model withholds the results it holds, while `--mode data` over a model that holds none cannot put them back.
Possible values:
- template: Structure and literals, without cached formula results
- data:     Everything, cached results included
- schema:   Structure and a column schema per region; no data-region values

Not combinable with `--exclude-section`.
